For many reasons, I don't believe in the GPT Store:
- In the Apple Store, most of the apps are free, while GPT users will need to pay $20/month. That might be a lot for many.
- I don't see a nice way right now to categorize GPTs too. How many apps do you use daily? After 10 you become overwhelmed. As a builder, it'll be hard to be among those 10 apps users need daily.
- Security issues. The most useful apps are usually personalized, not sure users will be comfortable uploading PII there.

comments.author: @dawid_dahl
comments.text:
Since there is almost nothing that these GPTs can do that regular ChatGPT cannot do (apart from having access to a few PDFs), I believe this will never become a new App Store. 

To actually create a valuable AI application these days you need to use more advanced RAG methodologies, create your own APIs and create functions to connect it the AI using OpenAI’s Function Calling, possibly fine-tune a model with brand new behavior, and/or often have a network of smaller AI’s working together in a complex web (in a performant and cost-effective way) to achieve some task.

Don’t believe the hype guys, I actually work as a backend developer and I know the only way to create an actually valuable AI app is to do something unique that ChatGPT cannot do on its own.

comments.author: @Jaybearno
comments.text:
I'm tripping out thinking about what OpenAI's macro strategy is for this. Sure, they open a dev community that can make cute bots, but how does that help OpenAI? Other than drive user engagement (something they need no help with) or run up the developers API call fees.

Since they only give Custom Agent access to Premium users, it might be reasonable that they distribute a share of the proportion of that users' traffic on your Agent / Total Monthly engagement. Depending on how they choose and value the engagement ratio could have big implications on how to optimize your agents profitability.

It's possible that the profitability of the agent is determined by these factors: [% of Premium Users traffic to your agent / Users total Usage] * [$19.99 subscription price]. I could see them assigning a fixed % of this, and reconcile on a monthly cadence.
Alternatively, they could just assign a flat value to tokens and determine what their margin is on them, then apply the royalty fee.
I could see there being a scenario where you want optimize both the types of users you attract, but also the cost effectiveness of the model calls and token volume.

Big picture for OpenAI, I can see this as their gambit to use distributed development to generate a massive training data set on API implementations, so that their next model will take all the data from community agents, fine-tune the next model with it, and lead to the ability to have  generically create it's own Agents, functions, and API's. This in effect is giving it the worlds biggest tool box to learn from., and could massively expand it's capabilities.

Is this making any sense to anyone or did my edible kick in and I should go to bed?
